title: Recording, mixing: Oh Woman, Oh Why, Sunshine Sometime by Paul McCartney | 1970
content:
Studio B, CBS Studio Building, New York City
Producer: Paul McCartney

Paul McCartney worked on two songs on 2 November 1970: ‘Oh Woman, Oh Why’ and ‘Sunshine Sometime’.

‘Oh Woman, Oh Why’ would become the b-side of his debut solo single ‘Another Day’, and ‘Sunshine Sometime’ was to remain an outtake until it was officially released on the 2012 reissue of Ram.

McCartney led the session musicians – guitarist Hugh McCracken and drummer Denny Seiwell – through rehearsals of ‘Oh Woman, Oh Why’, but no successful master was recorded, and it was decided that they would return to it another time.

The session ended with mixing work on ‘Sunshine Sometime’, which McCartney wanted to use in a mooted Rupert The Bear animated film. At the end of the day he took away a preliminary stereo mix.
